claims: DeFi eliminates intermediaries like banks by using automated smart contracts.
DeFi enables peer-to-peer lending.
DeFi enables peer-to-peer borrowing.
DeFi enables peer-to-peer trading.
DeFi operates on public ledgers.
DeFi applications use self-executing code on blockchains mostly Ethereum.
DeFi applications manage transactions automatically without intermediaries using self-executing code.
Users interact with DeFi services through decentralized applications (dApps).
DeFi dApps connect to crypto wallets.
DeFi dApps do not connect to bank servers.
DeFi uses user-contributed pools of funds for lending and trading.
PancakeSwap allows users to trade cryptocurrencies directly without a central authority.
SushiSwap allows users to trade cryptocurrencies directly without a central authority.
Curve Finance allows users to trade cryptocurrencies directly without a central authority.
Compound allows users to lend out assets for interest or borrow against their holdings.
DYdX allows users to lend out assets for interest or borrow against their holdings.
Stablecoins are digital assets pegged to fiat currencies.
Stablecoins are used to mitigate the high volatility of crypto markets.
Synthetic assets are tokenized derivatives that track the value of real-world assets.
DeFi is open to anyone with an internet connection and a digital wallet.
DeFi transactions are traceable and public on the blockchain.
DeFi platforms allow users to maintain control of their own assets.
DeFi primarily relies on cryptocurrencies as the underlying assets for various activities.
DeFi does not offer many of the consumer protections and remedies available for traditional financial transactions.
